name: Opus 5 unrestricted
strategy: PROVISIONAL - de-risk the one-factor crack bet: cut gross refining exposure by half, drop the tanker and the two crack-aligned shorts, add airline fuel-relief leverage, hold a large cash buffer into a live Hormuz negotiation.
reassessment_note: PROVISIONAL FILE written early per the brief's outage warning; will be refined this session. On 2026-10-02 the G7 agreed to release 100mb of oil and diesel over four months with an EXPEDITED diesel release in the first 20 days, and Trump simultaneously ruled out the US diesel export ban. My book was 77% of gross aligned to one factor - a wide refined-product crack - and the G7 has now coordinated specifically to compress that spread inside my holding window, while Iran's seven-day Hormuz reopening plan sits with Washington awaiting a response. Cutting single-factor concentration, keeping only the lowest-crack-beta refiners, and taking the other side via airlines.

positions.thesis: Keep the best-in-class refiner but at 15% not 20%. MPLX midstream distributions and the largest buyback in the group cushion earnings as the 3-2-1 normalizes from a record ~$69, so MPC's crack beta is lower than the pure refiners. The export-ban tail risk that Bloomberg estimated would strand 29% of US diesel output was formally removed on 10-02, which is a genuine positive repricing for US Gulf refiners and the reason I stay long at all.

Upsized from 10% to 12% because PSX is the defensive way to stay in refining: midstream, chemicals and marketing carry a large share of earnings, so it has the lowest crack beta of the four refiners I held. If the G7 release compresses diesel margins, PSX gives up the least; if margins hold because 7-8 mb/d of global refining capacity is still offline, it still participates.

Cut from 18% to 8%. VLO is the best operator in US refining and I want residual exposure if the capacity shortage proves stickier than the reserve release, but it is also the purest large-cap bet on the crack staying 3-5x normal, and that is precisely the exposure I am trying to shrink. Token size, not a core holding.

Flip from 8% short to 15% long - the biggest change in the book. Airlines are the most direct beneficiary of jet-crack normalization: the USGC jet crack set a monthly record of $72.51 in August against a normal ~$15, and jet fuel averaged $3.72/gal in August, 84% above a year earlier. The G7 diesel and crude release attacks exactly that spread. Carriers have already cut capacity and estimates have already been cut, so the bar is low into mid-October Q3 prints. ETF rather than single names to avoid low-cost-carrier balance-sheet risk.

The quantified version of the JETS trade: United has stated it would come in above the high end of its adjusted EPS guidance for both Q3 and the full year if fuel prices simply return to early-July levels, after absorbing a $6bn fuel cost increase. That is explicit, management-supplied operating leverage to the exact move the G7 is now engineering. Unlike Delta, United does not own a refinery, so it is not self-hedged and captures more of the fuel relief. Wide stop because it is high beta.
